components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; height: 320px; background: var(--color-enamel, #f6f7f4); color: var(--color-ink, #141816); padding: 16px; } .ds-plate { position: relative; width: 64px; height: 100%; border: 2px solid var(--color-ink, #141816); background: var(--color-plate, #fff); overflow: hidden; } .ds-face { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, var(--color-ink, #141816) 0 2px, transparent 2px 6px); background-size: 50% 100%; background-repeat: no-repeat; } .ds-m { position: absolute; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); background: var(--color-plate, #fff); padding: 0 2px; font: 700 15px/1 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; color: var(--color-danger-ink, #b3241d); } .ds-water { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; background: rgb(61 110 106 / 0.8); mix-blend-mode: multiply; transition: height 300ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-levels { position: relative; list-style: none; margin: 0 0 0 12px; padding: 0; width: 96px; height: 100%; } .ds-levels li { position: absolute; left: 0; transform: translateY(50%); } .ds-lvl { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font: 700 14px 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-tick { height: 2px; width: 10px; background: var(--color-ink, #141816); } .ds-lbl { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-lvl:hover { color: var(--color-water, #3d6e6a); } .ds-lvl:hover .ds-lbl, .ds-current .ds-lbl { opacity: 1; } .ds-current .ds-tick { width: 20px; } .ds-lvl:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--color-ink, #141816); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-tag { background: var(--color-ink, #141816); color: var(--color-enamel, #f6f7f4); padding: 0 4px; font: 700 13px 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: bottom 300ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }

narrative.overview:
The page is read against one painted river staff gauge, the white enamel plate a drainage authority bolts to a bridge pier. Each section is one metre on that plate, and the water rises as the reader goes down. Everything in the system comes from that object: an off-white ground read in daylight, black graduations and rules, teal water fields, and a few paint colours that only appear when they mean something on a gauge (the current reading, a high-water mark, the metre numerals).

Density is editorial rather than dashboard. A few very large wide-set statements, then long ruled records with condensed figures in a left column and prose on the right. Depth is flat: hard rules, square corners, solid fields. The only things that move are the water and its reading.

The world deliberately rejects the developer-portfolio default it replaced: no dark terminal, no hero card, no avatar, no badge wall, no card grid.
keyCharacteristics: Daylight enamel ground, never a dark theme; ink and water are the only large dark fields.
2px ink rules separate everything; there are no boxes with shadows and no rounded corners.
Two faces with fixed jobs: wide heavy Archivo states, condensed Barlow measures.
Colour from the gauge's paint carries meaning, never decoration.
One moving system: the water level and its reading, 300ms ease-out.

rules.name: The Paint Means Something Rule
rules.body: Green, red and amber are a gauge's paint. Green marks what is current, red marks metres and a high-water era, amber marks focus and reach on dark fields. If a use cannot be read as one of those, it does not get the colour.

rules.name: The No Threshold Strip Rule
rules.body: There is no green/amber/red alert-band strip. These readings have no thresholds, so the bands would claim a meaning the content does not have.

rules.name: The Ink Opacity Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy in text on enamel is ink at 100%, 75%, 70% or 60%. Do not introduce a separate grey token.

rules.name: The Measure Not Prose Rule
rules.body: Anything that is a number, a date, a period or a status is set as a Reading in Barlow Condensed. Sentences are never set in it.

rules.name: The Stretch Not Track Rule
rules.body: Big Archivo is made wide on the width axis (110% or 118%) and tightened slightly (-0.015em to -0.025em). It is never letter-spaced out.

rules.name: The Beside Not Above Rule
rules.body: A section's reading sits on the heading's baseline to the right, as a measurement of the section. Nothing small and uppercase sits above a heading.

rules.name: The One Column Of Figures Rule
rules.body: Dates and durations live in the 12.5rem left column of a record; prose lives to the right. Do not put figures inline at the start of prose.

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow or lifts on hover. A surface is distinguished by its fill and its rule, the way paint sits on enamel.

rules.name: The Gauge Mark Rule
rules.body: Bullets, markers and indicators are drawn as short horizontal bars, the same marks as graduations on the plate. Not dots, not glyphs, not icons.

dos: Do set every date, count, period and status as a Reading (Barlow Condensed, uppercase, tabular).
Do separate sections and rows with 2px ink rules and keep every corner square.
Do keep green for what is current, red for metres and high-water marks, and amber for focus and reach links on dark fields only.
Do put a new section on the gauge: add it to the rail's levels so the water and navigation stay one system.
Do keep motion to the water and its reading, 300ms on the water ease, and let reduced motion jump.
Do draw markers as short solid bars matching the gauge graduations.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients that model light, rounded corners, or hover lifts.
Don't add a green/amber/red threshold strip or colour-code content by alert level.
Don't use Warning Amber on the enamel ground, or Gauge Red for text (use Red Ink).
Don't set sentences in Barlow Condensed, or track Archivo out instead of stretching it.
Don't put a small uppercase label above a heading; a section's reading sits beside it.
Don't use cards, badge rows, avatars, a hero card, or a dark theme.
Don't take values from the root tokens.css; it belongs to the retired system.
